verdict.rationale: Bolt's docs say you can connect a GitHub repository to back up a project, sync commits automatically and work across branches. You can also create a new repo from a Bolt project or import an existing repo, and the full change history lives outside Bolt. That covers syncing to your own repository. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that commits made outside Bolt (e.g. pushed directly to GitHub) flow back into the Bolt project, since the docs frame the integration mainly as backup; independent or hands-on corroboration of two-way sync.
